# Janyris Cotto

Background in IT, networking, graphic & web design, and blockchain. Website: https://janyris.com/

## Cybersecurity projects

- [SOC lab: the legacy server breach](https://github.com/janyris/soc-legacy-server-breach): Incident response on a compromised legacy Linux server in an isolated VirtualBox lab, following PICERL. Found a backdoored FTP service (CVE-2011-2523) and a planted root shell, preserved evidence, contained and hardened the host, and wrote technical and executive reports.
- [Security+ (SY0-701) study guide](https://github.com/janyris/comptia-security-plus-prep): Free study guide I built while preparing for Security+: notes for all five domains, quick-reference sheets, and offline practice tools (scenario quiz, flashcards, acronym trainer).
- [Splunk Core Certified User study notes](https://github.com/janyris/splunk-core-certified-user-prep): Notes and 103 original practice questions I used to pass SPLK-1001, with every key fact linked to the Splunk documentation page that confirms it.

## AI in my work

I use Claude and Claude Code every day for research, documentation and scripting. I enjoy working with it, and I verify everything it produces before I rely on it. Long term, I am heading toward AI security.

- [AI-assisted analysis, manually verified](https://github.com/janyris/soc-legacy-server-breach): In the SOC lab I used AI to help plan scans, parse output, research CVEs and draft reports, and I checked every AI-suggested finding with a manual tool before accepting it as evidence.
- [AI-assisted study guides](https://github.com/janyris/splunk-core-certified-user-prep): Both certification guides were drafted with AI assistance while I studied, then fact-checked against the official exam objectives and vendor documentation.

## Log

- [SOC lab: the legacy server breach](https://janyris.com/#blog/soc-lab-legacy-server-breach) (2026-10-12): A legacy Ubuntu server was flagged for anomalous traffic. In an isolated VirtualBox host-only network, I scanned it from Kali and found about 25 open ports, including vsftpd 2.3.4 with its known backdoor (CVE-2011-2523) and a root shell already listening on port 1524. The scanner could only guess the FTP version because the banner was masked. A targeted script scan confirmed the real version. Taking the guess at face value would have mislabeled the entry point. I captured volatile state before isolating the host, then removed the backdoor, disabled xinetd, firewalled the entry point and verified the ports were closed. I wrote it up as a technical report and an executive briefing.
- [Security+ study guide is public](https://janyris.com/#blog/security-plus-study-guide) (2026-10-08): I passed CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) and published the study guide I built while preparing: notes for all five domains, reference sheets, and practice tools that work offline in a browser. It was written with AI assistance and organized by CompTIA's published objectives. It contains no real exam questions.
- [Splunk Core Certified User: passed](https://janyris.com/#blog/splunk-core-certified-user) (2026-10-06): I passed the Splunk Core Certified User (SPLK-1001) exam and shared the notes I used: one note per exam topic, an SPL command reference, and 103 original practice questions. The notes were drafted with AI assistance while I studied, then every key fact was checked against Splunk's official documentation and linked to the page that confirms it.
